The lines of a formation are like a language. I want to read it, and then write it myself.
The bustle of the hall tires me. On the quiet cliff I can hear my own qi.
The old map in the Scripture Pavilion has many blank spots. One day I will fill them in.
I saw a spirit beast track at the forest edge and could not stop thinking about it.
I counted the sect's spirit stones twice and found the difference. I think I have a head for trade.
The scrolls in the pavilion are kinder than people. I will read every one of them.
Someone has to stand at the gate while the others sleep. Let it be me.
A voice whispers that the ordinary path is too slow. I am listening to it.
I set down the old ways and lifted the sword. My hands shook, but my heart did not.

I started learning formations from the beginning. Cinnabar ink stains every sleeve I own.
I chose silence. From tomorrow I will sit on the cliff until my qi is still.
I packed a small bag. The world beyond the gate is too wide to only hear stories about.
I decided to become a hunter. The old bow in the storeroom is mine now.
I will trade. Spirit stones can also lead to the Dao, if they are counted honestly.
I moved to the pavilion. Those scrolls have waited for me longer than anyone.

kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.cit: Today I broke through to the realm I had dreamed of. My qi feels like a river that has just found the sea.
Something opened inside me. The Dao that was a blur now looks like a footpath under the moon.
The last form finally flowed without thought. Every technique I wanted is mine now.
I hold a treasure of my own. It feels warm, as if it had been waiting for me.
They shouted my name in the arena. I still cannot believe I am the champion.
I avenged that defeat. Strangely, what remains is not satisfaction but quiet.
I found someone who makes the sect days feel shorter.
Today I stood level with the master. They only smiled, and that was more than enough.
My robe changed colour. The juniors now call me senior.
My purse is finally as heavy as I dreamed. Now I must decide what it is all for.
A spirit beast chose to stay by my side. It sleeps at my feet tonight.
I came back from the secret realm with wounds and stories. I will carry both for a long time.
The people I helped waved as I left. That is worth more than any spirit stone.
My work is finished. I stared at it a long time looking for a flaw and found none.

kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.kej: A quiet day. I meditated, ate, and slept early.
I practised forms from dawn until the dew on the grass dried.
I sharpened my sword until it reflected my own face.
I noted the properties of three new herbs. One of them numbed my tongue.
I watered the herb garden before sunrise and talked to the sprouts.
I wrote twenty practice talismans. Only four did not fail.
I re-measured the formation eyes in the courtyard. One stone had shifted a finger-width.
I sat from morning until night. When I opened my eyes the moon was high.
I meditated under the waterfall. The cold was piercing, but my mind was clear.
I read old maps and marked the places I want to go.
A wanderer stopped by and told stories of a city beyond the mountains.
I practised reading tracks in the damp ground behind the sect.
I replaced my bowstring and oiled the wood.
I counted the spirit stones in my purse and planned my next shopping trip.
I wrote down the market prices I heard from passing merchants.
I copied a scroll that had begun to crumble. My hand aches, but the letters are neat.
I explained qi circulation to a junior. They finally nodded.
I kept watch all night. Nothing but owls and wind.
I swept leaves from the gate steps and greeted everyone who passed.
The whispers came again while I meditated. This time they called my name.
My shadow looked longer than usual. I told no one.
This evening I had tea with %2$s. We laughed until the lanterns were lit.
This evening I drank tea alone and watched the clouds.

kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.jal: Today I tied the sword cord at my waist and decided: the sword is my path.
A senior swung a sword in the courtyard and the leaves split in mid-air. From that moment I knew what I wanted.
I picked up a broken wooden sword from the storeroom and wrapped its grip in cloth. From today it is my companion.
Whenever I hold a sword grip my breathing evens out. Every other path feels like borrowed clothes.
The smell of herbs and cauldron smoke calms me. I think I was born to refine pills.
I peeked into the Medicine Pavilion and saw the cauldron fire change colour three times. I want to know its secret.
My nose knows the smell of spirit ginseng without looking. Perhaps it is a sign from heaven.
The first pill I watched being made looked like a little pearl. I want my own hands to make that pearl.
The lines of a formation are like a language. I want to read it, and then write it myself.
I counted the stones of the sect's guardian formation and found the pattern. My heart raced as if I had found treasure.
The formation senior drew one line and the whole courtyard shimmered. I want to be able to draw a line like that.
A twig on the ground, a stone in the corner, a shadow on the wall. Everything forms a formation if you look right.
The bustle of the hall tires me. On the quiet cliff I can hear my own qi.
I sat under the old tree and forgot lunch. It felt like coming home to a house I never knew.
The crickets are more honest than the chatter in the dining hall. I will find a quiet place to train.
The master says the Dao does not shout. So I will learn silence, so that I can hear it.
The old map in the Scripture Pavilion has many blank spots. One day I will fill them in.
I climbed the watchtower and saw blue mountains in the distance. I want to know what lies beyond them.
Every wanderer who stops by brings a story. One day I will be the one bringing stories home.
My shoes have never touched ground outside this valley. That has to change.
I saw a spirit beast track at the forest edge and could not stop thinking about it.
I waited two hours in a bush just to watch a spirit deer drink. Those were the best two hours of my life.
My ears catch a beast's steps before anyone else's. I think the forest is calling me.
The beast core the senior hunter brought home was still warm in my hand. I want to hunt on my own.
I counted the sect's spirit stones twice and found the difference. I think I have a head for trade.
I traded three bundles of herbs for a bottle of ink and still got change. The merchant stared at me a long time.
The numbers in the sect ledger speak to me like poetry. Strange, but that is how it is.
If I know the price of a pill in three towns, I know where to go. That is strength too.
The scrolls in the pavilion are kinder than people. I will read every one of them.
I found an ancestor's margin notes in an old scroll. It felt as if they were speaking to me directly.
The pavilion lantern went out and I kept reading by moonlight. I do not want to stop.
Every form has a reason, every reason has a root. I want to dig all the way to the root.
Someone has to stand at the gate while the others sleep. Let it be me.
I watched the old guard stand at the gate in the rain without moving. I want to be that steady.
When the juniors sleep soundly I feel at peace knowing someone keeps watch. Now it is my turn.
The sword is for striking, the shield is for protecting. I choose the shield.
A voice whispers that the ordinary path is too slow. I am listening to it.
In a dream I saw myself standing on a sea of violet fire. I was not afraid. That is exactly what frightens me.
Others need a hundred years. The whisper says I only need a hundred nights.
There is a book in the darkest corner of the pavilion that must not be opened. I have read two pages.
I set down the old ways and lifted the sword. My hands shook, but my heart did not.
The sword I once thought too heavy now fits my hand. Perhaps it is I who changed.
I asked a senior to teach me the basic stance. They laughed, then kicked my feet until it was right.
From today I rise before dawn for a thousand cuts. The old path I keep as a memory.
I asked for a place by the cauldron. The senior alchemist laughed, then handed me a broom.
My hands blistered at the first cauldron. But that small cracked pill was my own work.
I traded my forms manual for a herbal. I have read its first page seven times.
From now on my clothes will always smell of smoke. Strangely, I do not mind.
I started learning formations from the beginning. Cinnabar ink stains every sleeve I own.
I drew my first formation in the dirt and it glowed for an instant before going out. That instant was enough.
The formation senior gave me an old brush and said: a hesitant line will never glow.
I threw out the old plans and began memorising the eight trigram directions. My head is full of broken lines.
I chose silence. From tomorrow I will sit on the cliff until my qi is still.
I left the crowd and carried a mat to the cave behind the waterfall. Silence greeted me like an old friend.
My old ambitions felt like stones in a pocket. Today I took them out one by one.
I will become a recluse. The others may run; I will sit and let the Dao come on its own.
I packed a small bag. The world beyond the gate is too wide to only hear stories about.
I copied a map from the Scripture Pavilion and rolled it into my bag. From tomorrow the road is my teacher.
Sitting in the hall every day makes me restless. I choose the dusty road and the open sky.
I bought strong new shoes. The merchant says they can circle the world twice.
I decided to become a hunter. The old bow in the storeroom is mine now.
I learned to set snares from a senior hunter. My fingers got scratched, but my snare finally held tight.
The forest beyond the wall no longer frightens me. It is like a book waiting to be read track by track.
From today I eat from my own hunt. It is bound to taste better.
I will trade. Spirit stones can also lead to the Dao, if they are counted honestly.
I opened a little ledger with a red cover. First page: three spirit stones of capital and a lot of hope.
People say merchants have no Dao. I will prove that an honest scale is a Dao too.
I learned haggling from the kitchen aunt. She is fiercer than any elder.
I moved to the pavilion. Those scrolls have waited for me longer than anyone.
I rearranged the messy pavilion shelves. Behind the dust a world was waiting for me.
I hung my sword on the wall. From now on brush and scroll will keep me company.
The pavilion keeper gave me the key to the third shelf. I did not sleep all night from joy.
I chose to guard the sect. I will know this gate better than my own face.
I asked for the night watch and the old guard nodded without asking. They knew why.
I set my own ambitions down beneath the gate steps. From now on the sect's safety comes first.
I know the sound of every hinge on this gate. No intruder will pass without my hearing.
kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.cit: Today I broke through to the realm I had dreamed of. My qi feels like a river that has just found the sea.
The last thunder passed and I was still standing. The realm I dreamed of as a child is now the ground I stand on.
I write today's date large on this page. A new realm, the same sky, but my eyes see further.
The master says every realm is only a door. Tonight I walked through a door I once thought was a wall.
Something opened inside me. The Dao that was a blur now looks like a footpath under the moon.
A leaf fell, water flowed, and suddenly I understood. My Dao did not need finding, only acknowledging.
I stood beneath the pillar of light and spoke the name of my path aloud. Heaven did not refuse.
For years I asked what I was training for. Today the answer came without words.
The last form finally flowed without thought. Every technique I wanted is mine now.
The technique scrolls that once made my head spin now feel like songs I know by heart. They are all mine.
A senior challenged me to perform every one of my forms. They were silent a long time when I finished.
My hands move before my thoughts. They say that is the sign a technique is truly mastered.
I hold a treasure of my own. It feels warm, as if it had been waiting for me.
This treasure calls my name when I hold it. I will never let it go.
I spent the night gazing at my treasure's gleam under the lantern. It feels like a dream I can touch.
It took years, many spirit stones and more failures. But this treasure is finally mine.
They shouted my name in the arena. I still cannot believe I am the champion.
My last opponent bowed and conceded. The arena roared, and all I could think of was the master.
The champion's medal is heavier than it looks. Perhaps because every dawn practice hangs from it too.
The juniors carried me around the courtyard. I was embarrassed, but I did not want them to stop.
I avenged that defeat. Strangely, what remains is not satisfaction but quiet.
Their sword fell and they knelt. I lowered my weapon. The grudge turned out lighter once it was set down.
For years I carried that defeat. Today I repaid it, and then we had tea together. The world is strange.
They said I had changed a great deal. I answered: because of you. We both laughed bitterly.
I found someone who makes the sect days feel shorter.
We walked under the festival lanterns without saying much. No need; our hands were enough.
There is someone waiting for me to come home now. The cultivation path does not feel as lonely as before.
The seniors teased me all day. Let them. My heart is too full to be angry.
Today I stood level with the master. They only smiled, and that was more than enough.
In a friendly bout I held off every one of the master's forms. They patted my shoulder and said: it is time.
Once I could only see the master's back from afar. Today I stand beside them.
The master poured tea for me, not the other way round. I nearly spilled it from nerves.
My robe changed colour. The juniors now call me senior.
My new title was carved on the hall board. I touched it secretly when no one was looking.
A new rank, new responsibilities. The juniors now come to me with questions.
The elder handed me the badge and said: do not grow proud. I nodded, holding back a smile.
My purse is finally as heavy as I dreamed. Now I must decide what it is all for.
I counted my savings and laughed to myself. The poor child who once came through this gate would not believe it.
My purse is full. The first thing I bought was the finest tea for the master.
Wealth turns out to be a tool, not a goal. I only realised it after I had it.
A spirit beast chose to stay by my side. It sleeps at my feet tonight.
The spirit beast licked my hand and refused to leave. From today there are two of us.
I named it after thinking all night. It turned when I called, as if it had always known its name.
We trained together under the moon. Its breath and mine began to move as one.
I came back from the secret realm with wounds and stories. I will carry both for a long time.
The secret realm's door closed behind me. I came out carrying something I cannot tell.
Time moved strangely in there. I came out a day older but a year wiser.
I touched the differently coloured sky of the secret realm. I will dream of it for years.
The people I helped waved as I left. That is worth more than any spirit stone.
A village child gave me a wild flower as thanks. I have pressed it in this book.
They do not know my name, but they will remember our sect's robes. That is enough.
The master says cultivation without compassion is only patient greed. Today I understood what that means.
My work is finished. I stared at it a long time looking for a flaw and found none.
I put my mark on this work. Whoever uses it someday will know who made it.
A thousand failures before this one. Every one of them feels worth it now.
The master craftsman examined my work and was silent a long time. Then asked who my teacher was. I answered proudly.
kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.ibl: Tonight I heard the whispers again. They say my path is too slow, and I almost agree.
I saw my reflection in the pond and its eyes flashed violet. I turned away quickly.
There is a shortcut, the voice says. Only a little blood, a little of another's qi. I cover my ears but still hear.
I cannot sleep tonight. Every time I close my eyes I see myself at the summit with bloody hands.
I no longer fight the whispers. My qi is violet now, and it feels so strong.
I stepped over the line I once feared. On the other side there is only silence and power.
The juniors step aside when I pass. Let them. They do not understand yet.
The violet qi flows like hot wine. I know it is wrong, and I do not care.
The master sat before me and guided my breath until the whispers fell silent. I am ashamed, but I am home.
Golden light swallowed the violet fire in my chest. I wept like a child, and the master let me.
I was almost lost. The master pulled me back with patience. I will not waste it.
The whispers left, leaving a hollow that feels light. This morning the air smells fresher.
%2$s kept me company all night, talking about ordinary days. The whispers did not come tonight.
%2$s brought me warm porridge and sat until I finished it. Their hand never left my shoulder.
We played chess until late. %2$s lost on purpose, I know. The whispers did not dare come while they were here.
%2$s told stories of our first day at the sect. I laughed and forgot the voices.
kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.teg: The master scolded me today. I am annoyed, but the words keep ringing in my ears.
The master did not shout, only looked at me. That look was sharper than any sword.
I was scolded in front of the juniors. My face burned until night, but the master was right.
The master says a disciple never scolded is a disciple already forgotten. I choose to be grateful.
kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.puj: The master praised me in front of the others. I pretended to be calm, but I wanted to jump.
The master spoke my name in the hall. I bowed my head so no one would see my smile.
One sentence of praise from the master made this whole month's training feel light.
The juniors looked at me in awe after the master's praise. I must work harder to deserve it.
kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.sak: The sect treasury is empty; no pocket money this week. I will be frugal.
The steward shook their head when I came. The treasury is empty. Plain porridge for me this week.
No pocket money today. I comfort myself: even great recluses were once poor.
My purse is light and the sect is struggling. Perhaps I can help with extra work.
My pocket money was only partly paid. The treasury is tight, the steward says.
Only half my pocket money today. I set some aside for the master's tea anyway.
Pocket money was cut. The seniors grumbled, but I kept quiet; the treasury really is thin.
The steward gave me half and promised the rest later. I noted it in the corner of this book.
Pocket money for %3$s days came all at once: %2$s small stones. I counted it twice.
The steward poured %2$s small stones into my hand, %3$s days of pocket money at once. My purse nearly tore.
%3$s days of pocket money paid at once, %2$s small stones. My thoughts went straight to the town market.
%2$s small stones for %3$s days. I kept some under my pillow and some in my heart.
kultivator.sekte.mandiri.inti.harian.kej: A quiet day. I meditated, ate, and slept early.
Nothing special today, and that was pleasant. I swept my room, meditated, and slept.
An ordinary sect day. Warm morning porridge, a cool evening wind, my qi growing slowly like grass.
I went nowhere and did nothing grand. Sometimes that is cultivation too.
I practised forms from dawn until the dew on the grass dried.
A hundred opening forms before morning porridge. My legs shook, but my stance is getting lower.
Dawn found me on the training ground as usual. My shadow stretched and then shortened, and I was still training.
I repeated one movement until the sun was high. At last the wind at my fingertips made a sound.
I sharpened my sword until it reflected my own face.
Whetstone, water and patience. My sword can now cut a falling hair.
I cleaned a small speck of rust near the hilt. A sword well kept will never betray you.
The sound of the whetstone calms me. I sharpened until dusk without noticing.
I noted the properties of three new herbs. One of them numbed my tongue.
I drew a dew grass leaf in my notebook. Its veins turn out to form a formation pattern.
The senior alchemist checked my notes and corrected two mistakes. The rest were right.
I tasted the wrong root and my tongue stayed bitter until dinner. A lesson I will not forget.
I watered the herb garden before sunrise and talked to the sprouts.
I pulled weeds between the medicinal plants. A spirit ginseng sprout finally broke the soil.
Morning dew clung to the leaves like pearls. I watered gently so as not to knock them off.
The herb garden is in bloom. The spirit bees are busy, and I sat a long time watching them.
I wrote twenty practice talismans. Only four did not fail.
Half a bottle of cinnabar ink gone. The fifth talisman finally glowed before fading.
I practised the basic stroke a hundred times. The lines are starting to run straight without my holding my breath.
One talisman popped and singed the tip of my eyebrow. The seniors laughed until evening.
I re-measured the formation eyes in the courtyard. One stone had shifted a finger-width.
I ran a thread from formation eye to formation eye. All straight, except one which I fixed.
The guardian formation hummed softly when I touched it. I think it likes being cared for.
I redrew the courtyard formation diagram on paper. Now I know where every stone sits.
I sat from morning until night. When I opened my eyes the moon was high.
I closed my eyes when the rooster crowed and opened them when the crickets sang. My qi is calm as a lake.
My legs went numb, but the qi flow in my chest feels wider than yesterday.
A whole day sitting. I forgot to eat and was not hungry. The master says that is a good sign.
I meditated under the waterfall. The cold was piercing, but my mind was clear.
The waterfall beat on my shoulders like a thousand palms. I held on until my lips turned blue.
Behind the roar of the water there is silence. I found it today, only for a moment.
Little fish swam around my feet. They were not afraid; perhaps I have become like a stone.
I read old maps and marked the places I want to go.
I found a town I had never heard of on an old map. I circled it in red ink.
The roads on this map twist like veins. One day my feet will trace them.
I worked out the distance to the eastern mountains. Three days on foot, or half a day on a flying sword.
A wanderer stopped by and told stories of a city beyond the mountains.
The old wanderer told of a night market that sells moonlight in bottles. I want to see it.
A passing merchant told of bandits on the southern road. I noted it carefully.
I listened to travel tales until the lantern ran out of oil. The world is far bigger than our valley.
I practised reading tracks in the damp ground behind the sect.
I guessed animals from their tracks. Seven right, two wrong, and one turned out to be a senior's footprint.
Tracks in damp ground tell more than I expected: direction, speed, even fear.
I followed a spirit rabbit's trail to its burrow, then left without disturbing it.
I replaced my bowstring and oiled the wood.
I straightened the bent arrows one by one over a small fire.
My bow creaked softly. After oiling, it sounds like a sleeper's breath.
I fletched ten arrows with new feathers. My fingers were sticky with glue until night.
I counted the spirit stones in my purse and planned my next shopping trip.
I stacked the spirit stones in my purse in tens. Fewer than I hoped, more than yesterday.
I weighed it up: buy pills now, or save for a better sword? Tonight I have not decided.
One stone turned out cracked. I set it aside; perhaps a merchant will take it at half price.
I wrote down the market prices I heard from passing merchants.
Herb prices rose in the eastern town and fell in the western one. There is a lesson there, if I am clever enough.
A passing caravan sold spirit salt cheap. I wrote down the caravan master's name.
The price list in my book is three pages now. The seniors have started asking me before going to market.
I copied a scroll that had begun to crumble. My hand aches, but the letters are neat.
Ink dripped on the last character and I had to redo the page. Patience is training too.
This old scroll holds a long-forgotten form. I copied it slowly so it would not be lost.
The pavilion keeper praised my handwriting. I pretended it was nothing, but I was delighted.
I explained qi circulation to a junior. They finally nodded.
A junior asked why their qi kept stalling. I showed them where the knot was, and they smiled with relief.
Teaching turns out harder than learning. I have to understand something twice to explain it once.
The juniors gathered round me under the tree and listened. I felt like a little master.
I kept watch all night. Nothing but owls and wind.
The gate lantern swayed in the wind. I circled the wall three times before dawn.
A spirit fox peeked from the bushes, then ran when I greeted it. Otherwise the night was safe.
The stars shifted slowly above the watchtower. I counted them to stay awake.
I swept leaves from the gate steps and greeted everyone who passed.
The gate steps are spotless. A guest praised the sect's neatness, and I was secretly proud.
Dry leaves kept falling while I swept. The master says that is the lesson of patience.
I swept while reciting a sutra. When I finished, the broom and my breath moved as one.
The whispers came again while I meditated. This time they called my name.
The voice offered power at a cheap price. I refused, but my hands trembled.
Mid-meditation my qi veered toward the dark. I pulled it back with great effort.
The whisper knows my fears. It named my failures one by one.
My shadow looked longer than usual. I told no one.
The lantern in my room flickered violet for a moment. Perhaps it was only my tired eyes.
I dreamed of walking through an empty hall, every door opening into darkness.
The sect cat hissed when I walked past. It usually likes me.
This evening I had tea with %2$s. We laughed until the lanterns were lit.
%2$s brought flower tea from the garden. We talked about everything except cultivation, and it was lovely.
%2$s and I sat on the veranda guessing cloud shapes. %2$s always sees dragons.
Afternoon tea with %2$s. They told me about this week's failures and we laughed at them together.
This evening I drank tea alone and watched the clouds.
Warm tea, a dry biscuit and this diary. A simple afternoon, but enough.
I drank tea by the pond and watched the ripples the fish made. My thoughts grew calm too.
Alone with a cup of tea, I thought of my old home. Homesick, but not sad.
